title: EXACTLY How I Made $1M/Day Last Month (And What Went Wrong)

idea.name: Direct-to-consumer air filter manufacturing
idea.one_liner: Manufacture air filters in the US and sell them directly to consumers, earning revenue from product sales.
idea.customer: Consumers buying air filters; the transcript does not specify customer segments beyond direct-to-consumer.
idea.offer: Air filters manufactured in the US and delivered to end customers.

key_quotes.quote: I wanted to own a product that I could manufacture competitively in the US and sell direct to consumer in the US.

And my thesis was that then if I could do that, then I would have a long-term competitive advantage, and air filters fit that model because they are bulky and expensive to ship, which means like importing them isn't really realistic.

claims.claim: After 15 years building the company, it had reached a million dollars a day in sales.
claims.quote: After 15 years of building my company, we had finally hit a million dollars a day.

claims.claim: The company usually makes about $25 million per month.
claims.quote: I run Filterbuy, an air filter manufacturer that usually makes about 25 million dollars a month.

claims.claim: The company was on track to make $31 million in July.
claims.quote: But, back in July, we were on track to hit 31 million.

claims.claim: The business faced competitors with a 40-year head start.
claims.quote: The day I decided to start Filterbuy, I was going up against competitors with a 40-year head start.

claims.claim: It keeps less than two weeks of finished goods inventory across nine locations.
claims.quote: We keep less than two weeks of finished goods inventory across nine locations, and depending on how you look at it, that's either brilliant or insane.

claims.claim: It manufactures about 150,000 filters a day, seven days a week.
claims.quote: We manufacture about 150,000 pleated air filters every single day, seven days a week.

claims.claim: Orders average four or five filters per box.
claims.quote: And we ship those in an average of four or five a box.

claims.claim: It ships about 20,000 to 25,000 orders per day from nine locations, three of which manufacture products.
claims.quote: So we're shipping about 20 to 25,000 orders every single day from nine different shipping locations, three of which are manufacturing facilities.

claims.claim: On average, 80% of orders arrive the next day and nearly all arrive within two days.
claims.quote: These orders get delivered on average 80% next day, and basically 100% in two days.

claims.claim: Orders received by 2:00 are shipped the same day.
claims.quote: And if we're getting orders, you know, we're shipping them same day if they come in by 2:00.

claims.claim: He says distribution businesses usually average six to eight weeks of inventory.
claims.quote: And most companies that are in distribution average six to eight weeks of inventory, just to put it in a perspective.

claims.claim: The business replenishes inventory every day.
claims.quote: So that means that we had to be replenishing our inventory every single day.

claims.claim: On average, what sells in a day has to be made that day.
claims.quote: On average, whatever gets sold in a given day has to be made that day in order to keep up, and you have very little margin for error.

claims.claim: About 1,000 employees use its ERP system every day.
claims.quote: All of the things that keep the running and the operations going, like all thousand or so of our employees are using our ERP system every single day basically to tell them what they need to be focused on in that day.

claims.claim: He started building the ERP system from scratch 14 years earlier.
claims.quote: And I started that from scratch 14 years ago.

claims.claim: May revenue was about $23 million to $24 million.
claims.quote: We did 23 to 24 million dollars or so in May, which is about what we expected kind of ramping up into the summer season.

claims.claim: Sales grew for three consecutive weeks, each week bigger than the prior one.
claims.quote: 3 weeks in a row, bigger every time with zero promotion.

claims.claim: July sales came in 15% above forecast.
claims.quote: And so, what that ultimately ended up happening is July sales came in like 15% more than we had forecasted coming into it.

claims.claim: The unexpected 15% increase represented work equivalent to another 150 to 200 people.
claims.quote: Well, if you have to do 15% more essentially overnight than you expected, that's the equivalent of the work of another 150 to 200 people that you have to figure out how to basically make happen overnight.

claims.claim: July revenue exceeded $31 million, averaging about $1 million per day for the month.
claims.quote: But, ultimately, July sales closed at over $31 million, which means that we averaged a million dollars a day for the month of July and that was the first time that this ever happened.

claims.claim: It had previously had a $2.5 million sales day, but had not averaged $1 million per day for a month.
claims.quote: We'd had million dollar days, we've actually believe it or not had a two and a half million dollar day in the past, but we never averaged a million dollars a day over a month.

claims.claim: During the peak period, he was watching the business from 5:30 in the morning until 10:00 at night.
claims.quote: The only thing I could do was keep my eyes glued to the numbers on the dashboard from about 5:30 in the morning to 10:00 at night, it fully consumed me.

claims.claim: For about six weeks, his life ran through one screen.
claims.quote: For about 6 weeks, my entire life ran through one screen.

claims.claim: New Jersey and Toronto locations had opened within the prior six months.
claims.quote: And both New Jersey and Toronto, Canada were actually locations that have been opened up in the last 6 months.

claims.claim: The company faced $8 million in extra demand across nine plants.
claims.quote: $8 million in extra demand, nine plants, and what nearly broke us was one bad number.

claims.claim: It makes 150,000 units daily across hundreds of sizes.
claims.quote: Seems very simple or sounds very simple, but we manufacture 150,000 units a day across hundreds of sizes and multiple MERV ratings.

claims.claim: It has to deliver with 99.5% on-time delivery.
claims.quote: And by the way, you have to deliver your product or ship your product with a 99.5% on-time delivery, you can understand how it can get out of hand pretty quick.

claims.claim: For its first eight years, the business had one manufacturing plant and one shipping location.
claims.quote: In Talladega, I built the business for the first eight years with only one manufacturing plant, only one shipping location, right?

claims.claim: He spent about three months getting the New Kensington location running before handing it off.
claims.quote: Then I go to New Kensington in Pennsylvania where I probably spent the first three months getting it up and running and then handed off and then we opened up all these distribution centers.

claims.claim: His target is $365 million a year, equivalent to a million dollars a day.
claims.quote: It's been my goal for a while, at least from an ego perspective, to get to a million dollars a day, $365 million dollars a year.

claims.claim: The business continued averaging more than $1 million per day through mid-August.
claims.quote: We've been continuing to average over a million dollars a day up to mid-August as I'm filming this.

claims.claim: He says he understands the business better than he did 60 days earlier after spending six weeks deeply involved in it.
claims.quote: And I understand my own business better than I did 60 days ago because I spent six weeks with my hands all the way inside it instead of just looking at a summary.
